title: Contracts on the Move

intro.quote: “Think a different experience in mobile and tablet screens which don’t have to be the same experience as it is in desktop. This will reduce the cognitive load and improve the usability for the studios on the move.” — and Q-08 of the Quotes page: the next module is Contracts.
intro.method: A read-only audit of every Contracts screen at 390 (phone), 768 (tablet, portrait) and 1024 (tablet, landscape) with touch emulation, on a production build of tonight’s main — the Quotes-on-the-move build landed. Three lanes measured touch boxes, type sizes, truncation and sideways scroll, read the code behind each screen and sent, signed and deleted their own test records on a scratch database. Nothing of this is built. Your picks save as you make them.
facts: 62 shared shots + the lanes’ own at 390 · 768 · 1024
Build: main + Quotes on the move (REG-2525…2586)
answer: Yes — the same answer Quotes gave, with one surface that matters more than all the others. A contract on a phone opens as the thing the client gets (who it is for, which quote it names, where the link stands, the clauses as reading cards, one primary in a sticky foot); the editor comes on Edit as a short list, and the paper as a full-screen Document screen with one row of tools. A signature field is placed by choosing where, never by a thumb’s caret.

The surface that matters most is the client’s: today the signing page puts the form above the paper, the ticks 3,400px from the end of the reading, a code field without autofill, a pad that warps the stroke and a 4px thumbnail of the quote they are agreeing to. It should read like the confirmation page Quotes built — paper first, one bar that walks them to the signature in under two minutes. The pieces for most of this exist since this afternoon: the Quote screen’s shape, the section list, the paper viewer, the send sheet that fits, the picker as a list.

proposalTitle: The proposal: a contract you read first, edit second, and sign in one hand
proposalIntro: Six rules, then the screens drawn with OpenMaison’s own tokens, then each change as a card you can mark. Desktop stays exactly as it is; the data, rules and signing record are the same code behind a different order of screens. Where Quotes built the piece this afternoon, the card names it.

principles.title: Read first, edit second
principles.body: A contract opens as the document the client gets, with who it is for, which quote it names and where the link stands on top. Edit is a deliberate step.

principles.title: One primary per screen
principles.body: The filled button is the one thing this state needs next (Send · Remind · Download signed copy · Move to Won). Everything else sits behind ⋮ or in a sheet.

principles.title: One thing at a time
principles.body: Edit is a short list — Details, Document, Signature fields, Before the client signs, Automation — each its own screen, instead of a header, a meta row, a tool bar and 3,000px of prose in one scroll.

principles.title: A finger never places a field
principles.body: A signature field goes after a clause you choose, never at a thumb’s caret. A thumb reads, picks and signs; it does not aim.

principles.title: The client’s two minutes
principles.body: Paper first at 16px, a bar that says how far they are and what is next, the code autofilled, the signature typed or drawn at a fixed ratio, a signed page they can keep.

principles.title: Nothing is lost, it is one tap further
principles.body: Every desktop action stays reachable on a phone. Rare things move behind ⋮; the four things that change on site — the recipient, the date, the quote, a sentence — come to the thumb.

proposals.title: A contract opens as its document on a phone and a touch tablet
proposals.today: Opening a contract lands on the editor: a header of 184px (the title on two lines, chips, Saved, the status, Send), a meta row of four stacked blocks, a two-row tool bar — 520px before the first word, 80% of the first screen with the Sent banner. A Signed contract shows the same, with the bar greyed. Send is at the top of a 3,920px page.
proposals.proposed: A Contract screen (the Quote screen’s shape, `components/quotes/screen/*`, generalised): back · the client’s name with the title and the quote as the sub-line · ⋮ (grouped Look · Change · Share · Export). A hero: the status chip, From template, the contract date, the quote row (number · amount · status), the client row with Call · WhatsApp · Edit recipient. One Next line that says the link’s state (“With Olivia for signature — sent 20 min ago · not opened yet · link open until 29 Oct”). The clauses as reading cards split at the headings, the signature boxes as the last card. Folded rows: Signature fields · Before the client signs · Automation · Files · Activity. A sticky foot with Edit and the state’s one primary — Draft → Send · Sent → Remind (Send again once the link expired) · Signed → Download signed copy / Move to Won while the lead is not Won. “As printed” opens the house paper viewer; the Preview page at ≤767 is the reflowed paper under one bar with a Paper toggle (K3’s pattern).
proposals.why: the person opening a contract on site wants to know who it is for, whether it was opened and what to do next. The editor is for the desk. The pieces are built: the screen, the hero, the Next line, the folds, the foot and the viewer came with Quotes this afternoon; `lib/contracts/next-step.ts` is the quote’s on the contract’s states.

proposals.title: Edit is a short list, and Details is one form
proposals.today: The meta row stacks title · recipient · quote · date as four 44–56 blocks on a phone; at 768 it gives the title 0px and the recipient’s name 1px; at 1024 the title input is 140px for a 252px title. Everything is editable at once, under 192px of sticky chrome while typing.
proposals.proposed: Edit opens a section list (the quote’s `SectionList`): Details (title · recipient and their number · contract date · the quote · issued by — one form sheet, the four things that change on site) · Document (the paper, full-screen) · Signature fields · Before the client signs · Automation · Files — each with its one-line summary, so most rows never need opening. The address carries the step (`?edit=details`), so Back works. At 1024 landscape the list is a 300 pane beside the open section; held upright, a tablet follows the phone.
proposals.why: one thing at a time. The desk’s meta row is a desk piece: a phone gives each field its own line in a form and the hero shows the values.

proposals.title: The Document screen: the paper full-screen with one row of tools
proposals.today: The paper is a 3,000–3,800px contenteditable in the middle of the page under a two-row bar whose tools scroll sideways with no cut-off (seven of twelve hidden at 390); the Maison button covers the last 31px of every line; a chip’s “prints as” is hover-only; Insert a field is two levels deep. The same in the template editor.
proposals.proposed: Document (and a template’s clause) opens as the full-screen editor Quotes built for Terms (REG-2574, `Dialog phoneFull`): a 56 bar (← Document · the clause · Done) and one 44-pitch tool row — Undo · Text style ▾ · B · I · U · List · + ▾ (a sheet: Insert a field with its sample values · Add a signature field › · Link · Image · Highlight · Alignment · Numbered list). Nothing scrolls sideways, nothing hidden; the Outline (≡) jumps to a clause; no Maison button on this screen. A tap on a Smart Text chip opens “Client name · prints as Harpreet Kaur · Remove”. 768–1024: the same screen; the Outline is a pane.
proposals.why: a thumb can edit a sentence when the tools are one row at 44 and nothing covers the text. Hidden tools and a hover-only answer break “nothing is hover-only, nothing is cut” (REG-273).
shots: Today · 390: the bar ends at I
Today · a chip’s tap says nothing

proposals.title: A signature field is placed by choosing where, never by a thumb’s caret
proposals.today: eSignatures is an 88dvh sheet over the paper; Insert puts the field at the caret — with no caret, at the very end of the document, off-screen, with no message (a second press adds a second field); with a thumb’s caret, mid-word (“The con [CLIENT INITIAL] tract sum”) under the sheet. At 768 the drawer covers the place the field lands.
proposals.proposed: Add a signature field asks which (Studio · Client · initials, with “placed” marks) then where — the document’s clauses from the Outline (“After 11. Governing law and disputes” · “Under Signatures”, picked for you · “At the end”). It lands as its own block after that clause; the sheet closes, the box scrolls to mid-screen with the fresh pulse, the snackbar says “Client signature added under Signatures · Undo”. On touch a box has its own ✕. The eSignatures sheet splits into two folds on the Contract screen: Signature fields (placed / not placed · Add) and Before the client signs (the two switches as full-width label rows). At 1024 the pane is the placement list beside the paper, which slides left.
proposals.why: the desk rule “insert at the caret” (Dane UAT 8.03) is right for a mouse and wrong for a finger; a block after a clause is where a signature field goes anyway.
shots: Today · Insert with no caret: nothing visible
Today · the field inside a word

proposals.title: The client’s signing page: paper first, one bar that walks to the signature
proposals.today: On a phone the body is `column-reverse`: the first screen is the form card (eyebrow, “Sign this agreement”, the quote link, the read gate, the accept tick, the code, the pad, Sign) and the paper is 3,400px below; “Go to the box” scrolls back up. A two-document bundle takes four passes. The quote they agree to opens as an A4 zoomed to 0.45 — 4px type — in a new tab whose Back lands on a second agreement page.
proposals.proposed: The client page model Quotes built for the confirmation link: a 64 head (the studio · Secure signing); a 3-line hero card (the agreement · “Signs quotation OM-10008 · S$68,176 → As cards” · “Hi Vivien, read it, then sign with a one-time code”); the paper reflowed at 16px as today; a sticky bar — “Read to the end to sign · 3 of 11 sections” while reading, then Accept and sign (48, filled); the quote as the confirmation page’s reading cards in place, the A4 behind “As printed” in the paper viewer. After signing: the page lands on the signature box — “Signed · Save a copy · Pay the deposit · Signing record” — and the record is one tap away, not 3,800px down. A bundle walks its documents in order under the same bar.
proposals.why: the client reads before they sign; the bar tells them how far they are and does the next thing. The gates (read to the end, tick to accept — REG-633) stay exactly as rules; only where they sit on the screen changes.

proposals.title: The signing sheet: ticks, six code boxes with autofill, type or a fixed-ratio pad
proposals.today: The one-time code is a plain text field (no `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so the phone never offers the SMS); the pad is a 752×140 viewBox stretched to the card’s width — a square drawn at 390 is stored 1.97:1 and printed 62×34; Clear is a 36×20 text button in the pad’s corner; the NRIC field sits between the pad and Sign on every phone.
proposals.proposed: Accept and sign opens a bottom sheet in three screens, one filled button each: (1) the words to tick and the CaseTrust box; (2) the six code boxes (the house `CodeBoxes`, autofill from the SMS; the demo’s “any six digits” said plainly); (3) Type first (the name prefilled, the serif preview) with Draw one tap away — a full-width pad at a fixed 2:1 that stores what was drawn, Clear under it, “Add NRIC / FIN” folded. The consent sentence at 16. On Sign the sheet closes onto the signature box.
proposals.why: a signature a client cannot recognise as their own, and a code they must retype from another app, are the two moments a signing fails on a bus.

proposals.title: The lists as the phone card: the client first, what it signs, a read-only status
proposals.today: Four cards read “Interior Design Service Agreement”; the client is a 14px purple link on line 2 (absent on the lead’s tab); no amount; “Created” unlabelled; the only thing that opens the contract is the 248×20 title text; the status pill is live — one mis-tap marks a Draft Sent to Client or stops a client’s link.
proposals.proposed: The Quotes card (REG-2547): the client’s name 16/700 with the amount 18 at the right · “Signs OM-10008 · Interior Design Service Agreement” 14 · a read-only status chip with its since (“sent 2d ago · not opened” · “link expired” · “signed 12 Sep”) and a chevron. The whole card opens the contract; a long press selects. ⋮ = Open · Send a reminder (or Send the link again) · Copy link · Mark as signed… · Stop the signing link · Change status › · Share PDF · Archive · Delete. The to-do chips keep their words (“3 awaiting signature” · “1 link expired”). The lead’s tab: the same card with the title first. The Deleted and Archived sheets’ rows are the card.
proposals.why: a designer thinks of a contract by the client and the quote it signs, not by its template’s title; the status changes on the contract, where the rule can say why (Q-04 of Quotes, as picked).

proposals.title: Touch tablets open the tables with a default set, Title and ⋮ frozen
proposals.today: Both tables open every desktop column with the 555px Title floor: at 768 the frame is 642 and the row 1,700 — Title is the only column in view, the row’s ⋮ at x 1,733. `contracts-table.module.css` overrides the table core’s sticky actions under `hover: none`. The lead’s tab keeps the quick-links strip at 768 portrait. The gallery’s list view hides three columns.
proposals.proposed: The table core’s tablet default (`tabletHidden`, `useTableColumns(…, tablet)`, built for Quotes — REG-2549): Title · Lead · Status + since · Sent; Title and ⋮ frozen; View dropped (the title opens); the rest in Column settings remembered for the tablet. The module override of the sticky actions goes. No quick-links strip on the lead’s Contracts tab at 768 portrait (the Quotes rule). The templates gallery’s list takes the same default.
proposals.why: a table on a touch tablet shows what fits, never twelve columns (responsive.md § On the move). The piece exists; Contracts declares its columns.

proposals.title: New contract on a phone: who first, then the kind; the picker’s list on tablets too
proposals.today: “Which lead is this contract for?” is a 400 form with the house select: every lead, alphabetical, 44 rows, no search, no recent, a 690px list over the sheet. The picker on a phone was rebuilt this afternoon as a radio list and holds; on a tablet it still shows 414×328 cards whose 300px “paper” holds an 8px excerpt.
proposals.proposed: The Create Quote phone step (REG-2555): Who is it for? — recent leads first, a search — then the kind as rows: From the studio agreement · From a template (the list, the suggested one picked) · Import from file. The picker’s list goes to ≤1024 (the tablet’s cards are decoration that takes 70% of each card).
proposals.why: the lead first is how a designer starts anything on site; the list is already built.

proposals.title: A template is an outline you open one clause at a time; the gallery is a list
proposals.today: The gallery card is a 150×195 paper scaled ×0.25 (16 → 4px) with 12px facts under it, two per row, the folders first (the first template at y 416). The template editor is the contract editor: 416px of chrome, seven hidden tools, the FAB on the text, a 3,168px text box with no Done once scrolled.
proposals.proposed: The gallery on a phone is a list — Default and At handover pinned on top, each row name 16/600 · “13 headings · used by 5 · edited 14 Aug” 14 · chevron; the row opens the template’s reading screen: a 56 bar, a status row (“Default · used by 5 · fills 10 fields · client signs ✓”), the clauses as rows that open full-screen to fix a word (P-03’s Document screen), Signatures and Before the client signs as rows with switches. A standard PDF template keeps its picture with one Open the PDF (48). The row’s ⋮ = New contract from this template · Set as default · Use at handover · Rename · Move to folder · Duplicate · Delete.
proposals.why: a template on a phone is read, checked and corrected in a word — never written from nothing. A shrunk A4 says nothing; an outline says everything.

proposals.title: The contract inside the quote and the project
proposals.today: The quote’s *Contract · Sent to Client* was a 10px chip with a 20px touch box, and the Quote screen’s Next line ignored a live contract (it still said “send … for signature”, and Send ▾ would have raised a second one). The project’s signed contract is the eighth row of “View Client Info”; the contract value shows only inside a tile’s 12px help.
proposals.proposed: The Next line is the contract’s state once one exists and the primary is Open contract — built tonight as REG-2586 while the audit ran. Still to do: a 44 row “Contract · Sent to Client ›” under the quote’s hero; a Documents fold on the project Overview (the signed quote, the contract, each a 48 row with its date and ↗); the contract total at 14 in the To collect tile with its source.
proposals.why: knowing from the quote whether a contract is out, signed or missing is the question on site; a 10px chip does not answer it.

proposals.title: The Won step and Import take a photo of the paper the client just signed
proposals.today: The Won step’s “Attach client signed contract › Upload” is a “Drop your file or browse · Supports: PDF” box with `accept=".pdf"` and no `capture`: a phone’s camera is excluded, so the lead cannot be won with its contract from the phone. Files › Import refuses a photo the same way.
proposals.proposed: Two rows — Take a photo (capture) · Choose a file — on the Won step and on Import; the photo is kept as the signed copy (Files › Contract & VOs) and the lead moves to Won. The PDF stays what a desk uploads.
proposals.why: on site the client signs the paper, the designer photographs it and wins the lead — the one job the step exists for on a phone.
shots: Today · the Won step’s upload at 390

proposals.title: The scale 16 · 14 · 44 in every contract surface
proposals.today: Chips 10px (the only place the signing date appears at 390), Saved 12, the Send sheet’s subtitle 12 on four lines, deposit help 12, Automation help 12, the card’s since 12, the consent sentence the client agrees to 12, the CaseTrust bullets 12, the Filters chips 12, the calendar’s 32px cells, the client’s 36 buttons.
proposals.proposed: Quotes’ P-08 applied here: text people read at 16, secondary at 14, never under 14 for a value, a name or a sentence (a 12 uppercase eyebrow may label a group); amounts 18–26; every target 44, the foot’s and the client’s buttons 48; 16 gutters, 12 inside cards; inputs type at 16; the DateField’s calendar at 44 cells on a phone.
proposals.why: his rule after Quotes (responsive.md § On the move); the contract surfaces were built before it.

findingsTitle: What is wrong today, screen by screen
findingsIntro: Each finding names what was seen, where, and how bad. A finding the proposal already resolves says so and needs no pick. Severity: Blocker = can’t finish the job at that width · Major = hard, slow or error-prone · Minor = polish. The lanes’ full tables, measurements and shots are in the record folder.
findingsNote: most are covered by the proposal above; the rest are quick fixes you can pick

surfaces.title: Tools › Contracts and the lead’s Contracts tab
surfaces.intro: The list is where a designer between site visits looks for what is waiting on a client. Today’s phone card is the desktop row re-placed, and a touch tablet opens every desktop column.

findings.title: Four cards read the same title; the client is a small link
findings.what: Four cards read "Interior Design Service Agreement" (14/700, one line — "…Service Agr…" at 320); the client is line 2 as a 14px purple link (absent on the lead's tab); no amount anywhere; the date right is **Created**, unlabelled (a Signed card says "22 Oct ’26", not the signing day); no chevron. The card is the desktop row's cells re-placed, not the phone card Quotes built today.
findings.absorbedNote: the client leads the card, the amount beside it

findings.title: Only the title text opens the card
findings.what: The only way to open a contract is its title text: a 248×20 button (hit map 248×20). A tap anywhere else on the 358×134 card lands on `div[role=row]` and does nothing (`cardWhitespaceTap`). The ⋮ sheet has no Open row (Preview and Share · Copy Link · Mark as signed… · Download as PDF · Print · Archive · Delete); the comment in `contracts-table.module.css` says "View is in the kebab's own menu" — it is not.
findings.absorbedNote: the whole card opens

findings.title: The card’s status pill is live under a thumb
findings.what: "Draft ▾" / "Sent to Client ▾" on every card is live: a tap opens a Status sheet (Draft · Sent to Client · Signed); "Sent to Client" marks a Draft sent from the list (`setContractStatus`, no WhatsApp, the link now live), "Draft" on a sent one stops the client's link. One mis-tap on a list card changes a client-facing state.
findings.absorbedNote: the status is a read-only chip; the status changes on the contract

findings.title: Every desktop column opens on a touch tablet
findings.what: Every desktop column opens with the 555px Title floor: at 768 the frame is 642 and the row 1,700 — Title is the only column fully in view (Lead cut at 648+180), Status · Created · Signed Copy · Sent · Updated are off-screen; at 1024 (898 frame) Title · Lead · Status show, the rest not. The lead's tab at 768: frame 570, Title alone (Status starts at 648).
findings.absorbedNote: a tablet default set

findings.title: The row’s View · ⋮ sit 1,100px to the right at 768
findings.what: `contracts-table.module.css` `@media (hover: none)` overrides the table core's sticky `.actions` (parked at the visible edge) with `position: absolute; right: 0` plus a 150px band — the ⋮ sits at x 1733 of a 642 viewport at 768 (x 1553 on the lead's tab; x 1733 of 898 at 1024): a 1,090px sideways scroll to reach Copy link, Send a reminder, Stop the link, Mark as signed, Archive, Delete. REG-310 is the decision this copies (the listing's), but Quotes' tablet rule freezes ⋮ because the first screen must carry the actions.
findings.absorbedNote: Title and ⋮ frozen, View dropped

findings.title: The quick-links strip stays on the lead’s tab at 768 portrait
findings.what: The quick-links glyph strip stays (72×892 at x 688) and leaves the table 570 wide; Quotes hid it at 768 portrait.
findings.absorbedNote: no quick-links strip at 768 portrait

findings.title: The “Awaiting signature” chip collapses to a pencil and a number
findings.what: On ≤1024 the chip collapses to a pencil glyph + "3" (62×36, `ScopePill short`; its words live only in `aria-label` — a tooltip never fires on touch) and pushes the section title to "All Contr…" at 390 (88px, TRUNC) and "A." at 320 (18px). At 768 the row has 213px of title and still shows "✎ 3".
findings.absorbedNote: the to-do chips keep their words

findings.title: The card’s “since” line and the sheets’ status words read 12px
findings.what: "Sent just now · not opened" reads 12px (`.waiting` body-s); the Send-together rows' "Sent to Client" / "Draft" 12px; the Deleted sheet's note 12px.
findings.absorbedNote: the since line at 14

findings.title: Three stylesheets re-declare the house touch overlay and displace every 44 target
findings.what: Three module stylesheets re-declare the house overlay: `contracts-toolbar.module.css` 23–28 (`.menuWrap > span > button::after { inset: -4px }`), `contracts-table.module.css` 119–122 (`.float button::after { inset: -4px }`), `contracts-filters-modal.module.css` (`.foot button::after`). The house `::after` keeps its `translate(−22,−22)`, so the 44 box is displaced up-left: hit map −26…+36 on both axes at 390 and 768 — a thumb 4px right of or below the 36 glyph misses, 26px left/above hits.
findings.fix: Delete the three rules — `IconButton` and the DS md button already carry the centred 44 (REG-344, REG-2577).

findings.title: Filters keep the desktop rail inside the bottom sheet; chips read 12px
findings.what: The shared Filters shell keeps its 156px rail (Sort · Date · Status) beside a 234px pane inside the bottom sheet (panel 390×305); the Date chips read 12px (`Chips` label = subheading-s). A house piece (every Filters modal), said here because Contracts opens it.
findings.absorbedNote: the chips at 14; the Filters sheet in one column

findings.title: “Download as PDF” and “Print” both open the browser’s print dialog
findings.what: Both call `printPaper()` → the browser's print dialog (no file on this build); "Print" is a desk verb on a phone.
findings.fix: ≤767 one row **Share PDF** (the Quotes phone ⋮'s Preview / Share), Print only where a mouse is.

findings.title: A deleted contract is a stack of seven unlabelled lines
findings.what: A deleted contract is a 344px stack of seven unlabelled lines — the selection box, the title, "Serena Koh", "Draft", "22 Oct ’26", "Dane" (who deleted it and when read as bare words), then Restore 84×36 · Delete Forever 130×36. The trio's stylesheet (`deleted-contracts-sheet.module.css`, also Deleted / Archived Quotes).
findings.absorbedNote: the Deleted sheet’s row is the card

findings.title: Send together: with four documents the tools row drops below the fold
findings.what: The sheet is REG-2578's (the link row hidden, Copy link in the foot — holds). With four documents the message grows to 292px and Reset message · Write with AI land at y 943 (below an 844 screen; the body scrolls 228px under the foot — REG-2578 accepts it); the document rows truncate "Interior Design Service Agreem…" against "Sent to Client" / "Draft" 12px on the right; a document already out (Sent to Client) is listed and ticked again.
findings.fix: Rows wrap to two lines on ≤767 with the status under the title at 14; the message box folds to three lines with "Show all" on a phone.

surfaces.measure: Type: card title 14/700 · client 14 link · since 12 · chips 10 · the “Awaiting signature” chip 62×36 (a glyph + a number). Tablet: the Title floor 555, the row 1,700 in a 642 frame, ⋮ at x 1,733.

surfaces.title: New contract, Import, the picker
surfaces.intro: Starting a contract on a phone: the lead, then the kind. Today’s picker on a phone (rebuilt this afternoon as a radio list, REG-2579) holds; the tablet still shows the desktop cards, and the lead question is a 30-row select.

findings.title: “Which lead is this contract for?” is a 30-row select with no search
findings.what: A 400 form dialog with the house select: the list of every lead (30+ rows, 44 each, alphabetical, no search, no recent) opens 690px tall over the sheet; Continue is a second press.
findings.absorbedNote: who first: recent leads, a search

findings.title: The picker on a tablet still shows 414px cards with 8px previews
findings.what: The desktop cards stay: 328×414 (768) / 299×382 (1024) cards whose 300px grey "paper" holds an 8px excerpt — unreadable decoration taking 70% of each card; at 768 the dialog is 720×976 with the body scrolling (1,024 in 819) so the folders sit below the fold (y 851) under three cards; "Start from the studio agreement" + "Use template" are 36 in the foot.
findings.absorbedNote: the phone’s list goes to ≤1024

surfaces.title: The contract editor: frame, meta row, dialogs
surfaces.intro: The editor is the desk editor squeezed: at 390 the first word of the contract is at y 561; at 768 the title field is 0px wide and the recipient’s name 1px. Send lives at the top of a 3,900px page.

findings.title: The contract’s title field is 0px wide at 768
findings.what: The contract's title field is **0 px wide** (`titleField` w 0, its input 18 px): the meta row's `.titleInput { flex: 1; min-width: 0 }` gives everything to recipient (166) · quote (322) · date (200). The title cannot be read or changed at 768 — the header's title is the switch button, not an input. Signed at 768: the same 18 px.
findings.absorbedNote: the title is the Details form’s first field — and the hero’s

findings.title: The recipient’s name collapses to 1px at 768
findings.what: The recipient chip shows **"( · 9134 3428 ✎"** — the name span is **1 px** wide (`nameScrollW` 93): the chip's `min-width: 0` lets the name collapse to its ellipsis while the phone keeps `nowrap`. Signed: "Ryan D’…" (72 px). The recipient is the field a designer on site changes most.
findings.absorbedNote: the recipient is the hero’s client row and the Details form’s field

findings.title: 520px of chrome before the first word of the contract
findings.what: **520 px of chrome before the paper**: header 184 (title on two lines, chip, Saved, status + Send) + meta row 224 (title · recipient · quote · date stacked) + bar 112 (two rows) → the first word of the contract is at y 561 of 844; with the Sent banner (116 px, five lines) at y 677 — **80 % of the first screen is chrome**. The person opens a contract and sees no contract.
findings.absorbedNote: the Contract screen opens on the document

findings.title: Send lives at the top of a 3,920px page; nothing is sticky but the tool bar
findings.what: **Send lives in the header at the top of a 3,920 px page**; the header is not sticky at ≤767 (only the bar is). After touching clause 9 the primary is ~3,000 px away; after typing in clause 1 it is already at y −391. The status pill (89×36) and Send (257×36) are 36 drawn (REG-2577 keeps the 44 overlay), not the foot's 48.

findings.title: The contract value shows only inside a tile’s 12px help
findings.what: For an Owner the contract value shows only inside the To collect tile's help, "S$17,790.01 collected of S$81,355.42", at 12px; the breakdown ("Contract S$81,355 — signed quote + variation orders") is a hover `Tooltip` on the value and never shows on touch. A Designer gets a "Contract value" tile; an Owner on a phone gets a 12px aside. **Module-wide** StatTile help; the contract line is the project piece.
findings.absorbedNote: the contract total at 14 in the tile

findings.title: Files › Send for signature works; a photo of a signed page is refused
findings.what: The flow works on a phone (the row with its help, a 554 sheet, the kept file tile 146×153 with a 24 trash under the overlay, the switch row toggles as a whole, Import 77×36 / Cancel 79×36). Weak points: the subtitle is 48px of 12px text repeating the title; the dropzone (file removed) reads "Upload the contract PDF · PDF" and accepts `application/pdf` only, so a phone's camera is excluded.
findings.absorbedNote: the photo kept as the signed copy

findings.title: The Won step’s “Attach client signed contract” excludes the phone’s camera
findings.what: The box reads "Drop your file or browse · Supports: PDF" (desk words) and the input is `accept=".pdf,application/pdf"` with no `capture`: a phone's camera and photos are excluded, so the one artefact a designer has on site — the paper the client just signed — cannot be attached and the lead cannot be won with its contract from the phone. "From System" offers "Create Contract ›", which leaves the step. (The stage rail also scrolls sideways, sw 533 in 390, "New" hidden — the window is Leads'.)
findings.absorbedNote: Take a photo · Choose a file

questionsIntro: Where the proposal has more than one good answer. My recommendation is marked.

questions.title: Does a tablet in portrait (768) get the phone model, as Quotes does?
opts: The phone model with room: the Contract screen, the section list, the Document screen (Quotes’ Q-01, as picked)
The desktop editor with the meta-row and tool-bar fixes
Phone model up to 1024 in portrait; desktop only on landscape tablets

questions.title: The client’s signature on a phone: which comes first?
opts: Type first (the name prefilled, the serif preview), Draw one tap away at a fixed ratio
Draw first, as the desk does; Type as the alternative

questions.title: The status on a phone’s list card: read-only or live?
opts: A read-only chip; the status changes on the contract itself, where the rule can say why (Quotes’ Q-04, as picked)
The live pill as today, with a confirm on Sent to Client / Signed
Read-only on the card, Change status › in its ⋮ (as the Quotes card)

questions.title: The signed paper photographed on site — what is the signed copy?
opts: The photo itself, kept in Files › Contract & VOs as the signed copy; a PDF when the S34 PDF renderer lands (the developers’ seam)
Wait for the PDF renderer: refuse photos until a server-side PDF exists
Keep the photo and also print it into a PDF on the device (the browser print sheet — unreliable in WhatsApp’s browser)

questions.title: The client’s page: paper first with the sticky bar, or the form card first as today?
opts: Paper first; one bar that says how far they are and then Accept and sign
The form card first, as today, with the fixes to its pieces

questions.title: “Download a copy” for the client, until the PDF renderer exists?
opts: A signed page they can keep: “Save a copy” opens the phone’s share sheet where it exists, the signing record and the copy stay at their link; the PDF when the renderer lands
Keep the print sheet (nothing happens inside WhatsApp’s browser)
Email the copy from the studio (the house outbox) and say so on the page

questions.title: The one primary per contract state — this map?
opts: Draft → Send · Sent → Remind (Send again once the link expired) · Signed → Move to Won while the lead is not Won, else Download signed copy
Send stays the primary in every unsigned state
No primary on a Signed contract; Download and Move to Won both in ⋮

questions.title: After Contracts, which module next?
opts: Leads and Lead details — the module a designer lives in on the move (the listing is already right; the lead’s tabs and the Move stage window are not audited for the move yet)
Projects — the schedule, updates and money on site
